docs.text:
Welcome to the Math Tools Demo documentation!

This is a simple Python package that demonstrates how to build and deploy documentation.

def add(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Add two numbers together.

    Args:
        a: First number
        b: Second number

    Returns:
        The sum of a and b

    Example:
        > add(2, 3)
        5
    """
    return a + b

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
Statistical operations module.

This module provides basic statistical functions for data analysis.

docs.title: mean(values)
docs.text:
Calculate the arithmetic mean of a list of numbers.

The mean is calculated as the sum of all values divided by the count.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default values List[Union[int, float]]

A list of numeric values

required

Returns:

Type Description float

The arithmetic mean as a float

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the input list is empty

Examples:

>>> mean([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
3.0
>>> mean([10, 20, 30])
20.0
Source code in mypackage/statistics.py 
def mean(values: List[Union[int, float]]) -> float:
    """Calculate the arithmetic mean of a list of numbers.

    The mean is calculated as the sum of all values divided by the count.

    Args:
        values: A list of numeric values

    Returns:
        The arithmetic mean as a float

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the input list is empty

    Examples:
        >>> mean([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
        3.0
        >>> mean([10, 20, 30])
        20.0
    """
    if not values:
        raise ValueError("Cannot calculate mean of empty list")
    return sum(values) / len(values)

docs.title: standard_deviation(values)
docs.text:
Calculate the standard deviation of a list of numbers.

Standard deviation is the square root of variance and provides a measure of spread in the same units as the original data.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default values List[Union[int, float]]

A list of numeric values

required

Returns:

Type Description float

The standard deviation

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the input list is empty

See Also

variance: For the variance calculation

Examples:

>>> round(standard_deviation([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), 2)
1.41
Source code in mypackage/statistics.py 
def standard_deviation(values: List[Union[int, float]]) -> float:
    """Calculate the standard deviation of a list of numbers.

    Standard deviation is the square root of variance and provides a measure
    of spread in the same units as the original data.

    Args:
        values: A list of numeric values

    Returns:
        The standard deviation

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the input list is empty

    See Also:
        variance: For the variance calculation

    Examples:
        >>> round(standard_deviation([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), 2)
        1.41
    """
    return math.sqrt(variance(values))

docs.title: variance(values)
docs.text:
Calculate the population variance of a list of numbers.

Variance measures how far numbers in a dataset are spread out from their average value.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default values List[Union[int, float]]

A list of numeric values

required

Returns:

Type Description float

The population variance

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the input list is empty

Note

This calculates population variance (dividing by N), not sample variance (dividing by N-1).

Examples:

>>> variance([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
2.0
Source code in mypackage/statistics.py 
def variance(values: List[Union[int, float]]) -> float:
    """Calculate the population variance of a list of numbers.

    Variance measures how far numbers in a dataset are spread out
    from their average value.

    Args:
        values: A list of numeric values

    Returns:
        The population variance

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the input list is empty

    Note:
        This calculates population variance (dividing by N), not sample
        variance (dividing by N-1).

    Examples:
        >>> variance([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
        2.0
    """
    if not values:
        raise ValueError("Cannot calculate variance of empty list")

    avg = mean(values)
    return sum((x - avg) ** 2 for x in values) / len(values)
